executiveSummary: GM0546's 2025 identity, boundary, centre, 130,638 residents, 54 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, three stations and thirteen logical road-border links are coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Leiden is a dense historic city in Rijnland's managed boezem, with local Oude Rijn/canal, polder, sewer and regional defence dependencies; it is not hydraulically represented by an unqualified direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel or North Sea distance scalar. The canonical river preset holds 0.686733 m from T+24 through T+72 and coastal produces 1.902507 m at T+24 without a selected water level, defence section/failure, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Pluvial depth likewise lacks rainfall, terrain, sewer/catchment and control state. Seven nonzero individual presets place De Kooi first and share the same four largest neighbourhoods at the top, revealing population-led rather than mechanism-specific geography. Current Rijnland evidence on 2 September 2026 records KWA-light, low Rhine discharge, selective dike inspection and reversal of earlier drought measures; this is time-scoped operational context, not calibration for a hypothetical event. Public registers identify 51 water assets, two AWZIs, Liander/Dunea/Ziggo territories, one grid-planning sample, 155 antenna sites, 93 education records and LUMC, but not live topology, capacity, backup, acceptance or restoration. The N434's four logical municipality links represent one A4-A44 physical corridor, not four independent routes. Exact flood, service and T+72 recovery claims must be suppressed until governed local evidence exists; missing, empty or horizon-limited data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0546 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM0546 as Leiden in Zuid-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Hollands-Midden, and report 130,638 residents, density 5,978/km², 16.4% aged 65 or older and 42,159 one-person households. The reference point [4.48225548526772,52.151756086885335] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Fifty-four neighbourhoods in ten districts sum to 130,640 residents, two above the municipal total (+0.002%); published households sum to 74,245 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 21,435. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 130,638 without rewriting the observations.

BAG contributes one active place, Leiden, and BRT one woonkern, both contained by the generalized municipality. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0; annual residents do not measure students, commuters, visitors, rail users, event crowds, patients or other event-time occupants.

District-heating and public-charging values are missing in 54/54 neighbourhoods; home value, cars per household and several housing/benefit variables each omit one row. Publisher null, suppression or non-applicability remains NoData, not zero.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Omgevingsvisie Leiden 2040, 2026 climate/asset programme and neighbourhood sewer adaptation
evidenceSources.edition: Omgevingsvisie published in Gemeenteblad 2026 no. 47695 on 2 February 2026; 2026 programme and current project pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The official vision describes approximately 110 km of watercourses and identifies water nuisance, heat, drought and land subsidence as climate-adaptation dimensions. It applies the Zuid-Holland climate-adaptive building covenant to new construction and reserves public/open-water space for rainfall buffering. Policy is static planning context, not a flood footprint or completed protection.

The 2026 budget at https://programmabegroting.leiden.nl/beleidsbegroting/programmaplan/omgevingskwaliteit acknowledges no complete overview or full climate-risk assessment for municipal buildings and says monitoring is still being developed. It reports 18% of paved area disconnected from combined sewer in 2024 against a 20% 2026 target; these programme indicators do not establish current drainage capacity.

The current Gasthuiswijk/Haagweg-Zuid project page documents more frequent sewer overflow, street/basement water and delayed routing of rainwater toward Leiden's boezem. A project area and future design cannot be generalized citywide or treated as operational completion.

The official pages expose no blanket reuse licence. Preserve publisher, document/page version, access time, scope and planning evidence class rather than silently treating narrative as machine observations.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Rijnland water-overload playbook, boezem controls and Katwijk discharge asset
evidenceSources.edition: Current authority pages inspected 3 September 2026; page-level blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Rijnland distinguishes its surface-water duty from municipal sewer duty. Before or during heavy rain it can lower levels, run pumping stations at full power, deploy emergency pumps in a controlled manner so the boezem does not rise too quickly, use peak storage and discharge toward the North Sea or Hollandsche IJssel. These are conditional response options, not confirmed actions in every simulation.

The Rijnland boezem is a managed regional system. Local canals, Oude Rijn water and polder drainage therefore require catchments, boundary levels, controls and authority state rather than a generic major-river proximity value.

Boezemgemaal Katwijk drains the regional boezem through the Katwijk canal toward the North Sea. Its published static capacity is 94 m³/s, with a further 75 m³/s possible at high sea levels; capacity is not live output, available reserve, Leiden-only protection or proof of current operation.
A defensible flood run must keep rainfall/pluvial, boezem overload, regional freshwater operations, primary/regional defence failure and direct North Sea surge as distinct mechanisms.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Time-scoped drought and freshwater operational update
evidenceSources.edition: Operational update dated 2 September 2026; validity is the published situation, not an evergreen state; page-level blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: As published 2 September, recent rain had improved conditions and there was enough freshwater to maintain levels, but drought was not over, Rhine discharge remained low and freshwater availability remained under pressure. KWA-light remained active and could be adjusted as circumstances changed.

The salt-control barrier placed in Leidsevaart on 5 August was removed on 2 September after water quality improved. Rijnland continued inspection at the most risk-prone dike locations; existing damage could still deteriorate. These dated actions must not be persisted past their validity without refresh.

Earlier 2026 measures included switching off Katwijk/Halfweg/Spaarndam pumps, up to 15 m³/s KWA supply, altered levels/flows and navigation restrictions. The timeline explicitly records change; historic states are not current T0 truth.

The current update is source-backed operational context but is not a Leiden-specific water-level observation, hydraulic initial condition or authority-selected disaster scenario. It should remain affectsSimulation=false unless a governed adapter defines issue/valid time, geometry, variable, units and event boundary.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Public water-asset registers and Leiden wastewater-treatment energy context
evidenceSources.edition: HWH snapshots retrieved 3 September 2026 01:38Z; current Rijnland wastewater page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The deployed CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH services contain 51 points clipped to GM0546: AWZI Leiden Noord, AWZI Leiden Zuid-West, 37 surface-water pumps and 12 sluices. Forty-nine name Rijnland and two generic Waterschap; 24 capacities are non-null and 27 are null. Status 'gerealiseerd' does not establish present operation.

No HWH sewer-pump or weir point appears in the bounded clip. HWH is contributor-dependent partial coverage, so an empty class is not proof of absence. Point location, free-text name, manager and capacity do not supply catchment, connectivity, unit comparability, control state, power/telecom dependencies, backup or recovery.

Rijnland says Leiden Noord and Leiden Zuidwest generate all their heat demand and approximately 50% of electricity consumption on-site. This is static resilience context, not evidence of islanding, fuel/sludge availability, black start, current output or backup endurance.

The deployed public Waterinfo layer returns zero local observations and forecasts because it covers selected Rijkswaterstaat waters, not all Rijnland assets or canals. No local match is NoData/out-of-coverage, not normal level or safe water.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB roads, rail/scheduled transit and N434 Corbulotunnel identity
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; ProRail and OVapi snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; current N434 page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates thirteen logical municipality links: A44 twice, A4 three times, N11 once, N206 twice, N434 four times and N447 once. Repeated links with one physicalCorridorId are boundary/series representations with generalized 260/150 scenario ceilings, never additive measured traffic or emergency throughput.

Rijkswaterstaat says the approximately 4 km N434 connects A44 and A4, includes a 2.5 km Corbulotunnel and 1.4 km depressed section, opened 5 July 2024, and is monitored 24/7. It can close for maintenance, faults or damage; static identity and monitoring do not establish event-time passability.

The four GM0546 N434 links point to Leidschendam-Voorburg, Voorschoten, Wassenaar and Katwijk but all share NWB-road-434: one physical A4-A44 corridor, not four independent Leiden evacuation/supply exits. The dated September 2026 planned maintenance lies after the audit T0+72 window and must not be applied early.

ProRail locates Leiden Centraal, De Vink and Leiden Lammenschans; GTFS yields 158 stop areas. Geometry and schedules do not establish operation, crowding, accessibility, ambulance/freight throughput, bridge/tunnel inspection or restoration. Zero bounded NDW matches never means all roads are open.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Leiden local risk profile, crisis preparation and 72-hour emergency-support pilot
evidenceSources.edition: Current public risk and crisis pages plus First Progress Report 2026 inspected 3 September 2026; edition/cadence and blanket reuse licence not stated on the local risk page
supports: VRHM describes compact, dense Leiden's centre role, historic canals/singels, large visitor-drawing events and the Stationspleintunnel near Leiden Centraal as an access dependency for LUMC. It identifies A4, A44, N11 and N206 as routes whose incidents can strongly affect access; the profile predates or omits explicit N434 treatment.

The Bio Science Park crosses Leiden and Oegstgeest and adds technological/hazardous-material dependencies. It must remain separate from natural-disaster forcing while its access, occupants and care/lab continuity may be common consequences.

Leiden's current page at https://gemeente.leiden.nl/voorbereiden-op-een-crisis/ advises a 72-hour household kit/plan and mutual help because power, water and internet may fail and responders prioritize acute danger. Guidance is not measured household stock, guaranteed response or a recovery deadline.

The 2026 progress report says Leiden started a VRHM pilot around a 72-hour power-outage scenario to develop and exercise a local emergency-support point. Pilot intent is not a named, staffed, powered, supplied or activated facility.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Acute care, provider territories, grid-planning, communications and education context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026; provider/register/planning snapshots retrieved in 2026
supports: RIVM CC0 v1.1 identifies LUMC inside GM0546 as 24/7 SEH and acute-obstetrics provider with 17 reported rooms and 22,493 visits in 2025. It identifies Alrijne Leiderdorp 4.1 km outside as another 24/7 provider with 20 rooms and 33,265 visits. Annual questionnaire data are not live acceptance, occupancy, staffing, backup, diversion or incident capacity.

The Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting point lookup at the municipal reference point identifies Liander electricity and gas, Dunea drinking water and Ziggo telecom, with provider update dates from September 2025 to May 2026; drainage returns empty. A single point is not municipality-wide coverage, physical topology, outage or restoration.

One Liander planning sample, OS LEIDEN ZUID WEST 10-1i, reports withdrawal 40 MW existing/43 required and 8.8 MW across 15 queued requests; injection 40/16 MW and 15 MW queued, with 14 projects earliest 2026. NBNL planning cadence is at least quarterly/queues monthly and exact dataset licence was not found; it is not live load, spare capacity, outage or T+72 availability.

RDI returns 155 antenna sites and DUO 93 education records. RDI states neither a fixed refresh nor reuse licence in the consumed metadata; daily DUO RIO uses CC BY without a version stated. Sites and institution locations do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, shelter role, occupancy, staff or supplies. A GTFS stop named Alrijne Ziekenhuis in Leiden must not be conflated with the RIVM acute-care site in Leiderdorp.

emergencyContext.summary: Authorities, local risks, preparedness guidance and care roles are identified, but no auditable T0–T+72 action/resource state drives the model.

LUMC and external Alrijne provide dated role context, not guaranteed acceptance, backup, staffing, supply or access.

notes: Mandatory and focused runs cover T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Affected population is a synthetic people-equivalent index, not observed persons, casualties or evacuations; person-hours is weighted local service deprivation against a matched no-event baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, zero-event baseline, reconciliation, causal arithmetic and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0546 pnpm audit:model passed 2/2 focused coverage tests in 29.82 seconds.
A separate diagnostic probe enumerated T+24/T+72 outputs and passed in 14.10 seconds; temporary files were removed.
All availability values remain in [0,1], UI and sim-core preset factories agree, repeat runs are exact, local demand/delivery reconciles and event-attributable person-hours is monotonic.
Arithmetic validity cannot turn planning, static registers or an unselected generic preset into local measurement or forecast.

spatialPlausibility.summary: River/coastal/pluvial scalars lack Leiden hydraulic geometry, and distinct hazards reuse a population-led neighbourhood order.
notes: River holds exactly floodDepthM 0.686733 and severity 0.215537 from T+24 through T+72 without a named major-river/boezem event, level/datum, defence state, footprint, arrival or recession.

Coastal T+24 gives 1.902507 m and 82,698 affected without a North Sea level/surge, defence section/failure or connected inundation surface. Leiden is inland and protected, but a supported defence-failure scenario could still flood it; absence of that scenario is Unknown, not safe.
Pluvial T+24 gives 0.558127 m and 29,735 affected without a rainfall hyetograph, terrain/depression field, imperviousness, groundwater, sewer/catchment or pump/receiving-boezem state.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter and cyber all rank De Kooi first and contain the same four largest neighbourhoods in their top four, with most top-eight sets nearly identical. Earthquake and wildfire direct exposure are zero at T+24; neither is an all-clear.

notes: River T+24 availability is power 0.706300, water 0.682207, drainage 0.580010, gas 0.828503, telecom 0.664707, mobility 0.771933, facilities 0.753612 and supply 0.740823; no operator validates these exact values.

Coastal T+24 availability is power 0.310355, water 0.403814, drainage 0.236833, gas 0.657667, telecom 0.289046, mobility 0.486804, facilities 0.324037 and supply 0.647055; these are aggregate synthetic percentages.

HWH points, partial AWZI energy generation, provider territories, one NBNL planning point, antenna sites, stations/stops and acute-care registration supply context but no live connectivity, load/flow, quality, backup, switching, staff, stock, crew or repair state.
NWB links may drive only mobility/road-logistics supply under transparent assumptions; they must not become power, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom or care topology.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic ledgers close, but unresolved hydraulic, target, lifeline and action dimensions are not honestly gating the displayed consequences.
notes: Hazard contributions, service-stage deltas and weighted service-loss contributions reconcile, and public planning/context layers remain non-causal.
No selected source event supplies water level/datum, rainfall, defence/control state, local footprint, fire source/perimeter, cyber target, operator outage, hospital acceptance or authority action.
The 2 September drought update has source/valid time and records changed operations; it cannot silently persist or calibrate a generic heat/river/compound run.
Unsupported exact depth, affected and service values must be marked synthetic screening/Unknown locally and declare missing dimensions next to maps, briefs and exports.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent and recovering impacts through T+72 are deterministic but unsupported by hydraulics, operators, routes, care state or confirmed actions.
notes: River retains floodDepthM 0.686733 and severity 0.215537 through T+72; affected rises 26,277 to 29,498 and pressure 0.282768 to 0.300269 while every service except facilities is exactly unchanged and facilities falls 0.753612 to 0.628602. Burden reaches 2,520,423.62 without hydraulic or operational cause.
Coastal direct hazard clears by T+72 but 28,211 affected people-equivalent, pressure 0.293279 and burden 5,077,316.98 remain without recession, dewatering, inspection, repair or care evidence.

Compound severity falls 0.921385 to 0.561254 while floodDepthM 0.577629, 88,064 affected, pressure 0.618468 and all eight service values remain exactly at their T+24 levels; burden reaches 5,546,408.66.

Only confirmed, validity-aligned water-control, warning, inspection, restriction, care, utility, logistics and welfare actions may alter recovery. Seventy-two hours is preparedness scope, not a promise of restoration.

findings.action: Suppress decision-facing river depth, affected counts, percentages and hotspot claims until a governed scenario distinguishes main-river boundary, KWA/Oude Rijn/boezem and polder pathways and binds water level/discharge, datum, defences, controls, footprint, timing, uncertainty and NoData. Do not suppress general flood preparedness.

findings.action: Gate direct coastal consequences behind a named authority-approved LIWO/defence scenario with release, sea boundary, breach/overtopping, footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability and uncertainty. Without it show direct impact Unknown/unsupported, not zero risk.

findings.summary: Pluvial output omits the dense city's sewer, surface and boezem-control mechanisms.

findings.action: Integrate a governed Leiden/Rijnland climate-stress or hydraulic surface with KNMI hyetograph, AHN/BGT, sewer-included flag, groundwater/saturation, catchments, pumps and receiving-boezem level. Wildfire T+24 has zero direct fire/affected but nonzero smoke/drought/service burden; earthquake has zero ground motion/affected but nonzero burden.
